name: Immunotactoid Glomerulopathy

criteria.description: Renal biopsy showing organized microtubular deposits with diameter >30 nm on electron microscopy
Presence of monoclonal or polyclonal immunoglobulin deposits on immunofluorescence microscopy
Proteinuria and/or nephrotic syndrome with or without renal insufficiency
Negative Congo red staining to exclude amyloidosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic microtubular deposits on electron microscopy plus compatible immunofluorescence findings and clinical presentation of proteinuria or nephrotic syndrome
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires renal biopsy with electron microscopy; differentiation from fibrillary glomerulonephritis is critical.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Electron microscopy revealing microtubular deposits >30 nm

occasional.symptomName: Fatigue related to chronic kidney disease
searchTerms: fatigue linked to chronic kidney failure
low energy due to kidney problems

occasional.notes: May be related to systemic immune dysregulation
Low complement levels in some cases

laboratory: Possible monoclonal gammopathy on serum protein electrophoresis
Low complement levels in some cases
imaging: Electron microscopy showing microtubular deposits >30 nm in diameter
Light microscopy with mesangial expansion and capillary wall thickening
genetic: No known specific genetic mutations identified
other: Negative Congo red stain to exclude amyloidosis
Immunofluorescence showing IgG and complement deposits

distinguishingFeatures: Fibrillary deposits smaller (12-24 nm) and randomly arranged
Negative or weak staining for DNAJB9
No organized microtubular structures on electron microscopy
Congo red positive deposits with apple-green birefringence
Non-organized fibrillar deposits of 8-12 nm diameter

redFlags: Nephrotic syndrome refractory to standard therapy
Presence of monoclonal gammopathy or hematologic malignancy
references: Nasr SH, et al. Immunotactoid glomerulopathy: clinicopathologic features and long-term outcomes. Kidney Int. 2011;80(9):1001-1009.
Sethi S, et al. Fibrillary and immunotactoid glomerulonephritis: distinct entities with different clinical and pathologic features. Kidney Int. 2013;83(4):684-692.
